findings.title: getCalendarCredentials returns Promise values from a synchronous function
findings.body: After the async refactor, `getCalendar(credential)` now returns `Promise<Calendar | null>`, but `getCalendarCredentials` is still declared as a synchronous function and pushes that Promise into the returned objects as `calendar`. This silently changes the public contract of the exported function: callers that previously received a `Calendar | null` now receive an unawaited Promise, and any new caller (and any existing caller that does not already do `await item.calendar`) will silently treat the Promise as truthy and call methods on it, causing runtime TypeErrors. `getCalendarCredentials` should be made `async` (or the calendar should be awaited inside the flatMap) so the returned `calendar` field is always `Calendar | null`.

findings.title: forEach(async ...) swallows errors from getCalendar in recurring cancellation path
findings.body: Lines 457-470 use `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... })`. `Array.prototype.forEach` does not await async callbacks, and there is no try/catch around the dynamic import. If `await getCalendar(credential)` rejects (for example because one of the calendar app modules fails to load), the rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection rather than being routed to the existing `logger.error`/cancellation logic, and the corresponding calendar entries are never deleted. The booking is marked cancelled in the DB while the actual calendar event remains. The surrounding `try/catch` at lines 135-139 (in the reschedule files) gives the false impression that errors are caught — they are not, because async callback errors from forEach escape. The same pattern exists in other files modified by this PR.

findings.title: forEach(async ...) in vital reschedule swallows getCalendar failures
findings.body: Line 125 wraps the reference-cancellation loop in `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... })` inside a `try { ... } catch` block. forEach does not await async callbacks, so a rejection from the dynamic import (`getCalendar` → `appStore[calendarType]` → `import("./...")`) propagates as an unhandled promise rejection rather than being caught by the surrounding try/catch (which only sees sync throws and the resolved values of the inner promises). The reschedule returns success even when calendar delete calls never executed, leaving stale calendar events on the user's calendars.

findings.title: forEach(async ...) in wipemycalother reschedule swallows getCalendar failures
findings.body: Same pattern as in `packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts`: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... })` inside a try/catch. forEach does not await async callbacks, so any rejection from `await getCalendar` (caused by a broken app module or a missing dependency) is not routed to the existing `logger.error` branch and becomes an unhandled rejection. Calendar/video deletions can silently fail.

findings.title: forEach(async ...) in requestReschedule swallows getCalendar failures
findings.body: Lines 553-567 fire calendar/video deletions with `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })` and there is no try/catch at all in this scope. Because forEach does not await the async callback, a rejection from `await getCalendar` (from the now-dynamic `appStore[...]` import) becomes an unhandled rejection. The mutation returns success while the prior calendar events on the attendee/organizer calendars may never have been deleted, leading to stale events being shown on those calendars after a reschedule.

findings.title: getCalendar does not handle dynamic-import failures
findings.body: Line 15 awaits the dynamic import directly: `const calendarApp = await appStore[calendarType.split("_").join("") as keyof typeof appStore];`. After the PR, `appStore` values are dynamic-import Promises that can reject if the underlying module fails to evaluate (bad syntax, missing dependency, server-side import error, etc.). There is no try/catch around the await, so any such failure propagates and aborts the whole calendar operation (booking creation, cancellation, reschedule, busy-time fetch). The existing post-await guard only handles the `undefined` / missing-`lib` case. The function should catch import errors, log them, and return `null` so that one broken app module doesn't take down operations for users who don't even use that app.

findings.title: getCachedResults awaits all getCalendar calls sequentially inside the map
findings.body: In `getCachedResults`, the calendars are now loaded with `await Promise.all(calendarCredentials.map((credential) => getCalendar(credential)))`, which is correctly parallelized. However the subsequent `results = calendars.map(async (c, i) => { ... })` then immediately awaits via `Promise.all`, which is fine. The new `getCalendarCredentials` function on the other hand still loads calendars sequentially (one `flatMap` callback at a time), and the `getVideoAdapters` factory in `packages/core/videoClient.ts` was also rewritten as a serial `for` loop rather than a `Promise.all` over credentials. For tenants with several credentials the first booking/cancellation pays N×(module-fetch latency) serially; parallelizing the per-credential fetches would substantially reduce tail latency of the first request after a cold start.

findings.title: No tests added for the async app-store refactor
findings.body: This PR converts a large surface area of calendar/video/payment loaders from synchronous to dynamic-import-based, including `getCalendar`, `getVideoAdapters`, `getCalendarCredentials`, the reschedule handlers in `vital` and `wipemycalother`, the cancellation handlers in `handleCancelBooking`, the `requestReschedule` tRPC mutation, the `confirm` mutation's refund path, and both `handlePayment` and `deletePayment`. Despite touching every booking lifecycle path, no test files are added or modified in the diff. There is no coverage that the now-dynamic imports resolve and behave identically, that error paths (missing app, broken module) return null instead of throwing, or that the new `await` placements actually preserve execution ordering. Given the scale of the refactor, this is a significant test gap.
